summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass complicated by post-bypass hypoglycemia requiring a gastrostomy tube and later bypass reversal was readmitted three days after a norovirus hospitalization for persistent nausea, non-bloody/non-bilious vomiting, watery non-bloody diarrhea, poor oral intake, and dehydration. Evaluation showed stable vital signs and reassuring labs aside from mild AST elevation; given recent confirmed norovirus and no new red flags, stool studies and imaging were not repeated, and bariatric surgery recommended symptomatic management. She was treated with IV fluids, close electrolyte monitoring without need for repletion, scheduled ondansetron with prochlorperazine as needed, avoidance of loperamide due to prior symptom worsening, and gradual diet advancement from clear liquids to soft/regular diet with oral supplements; tube feeds were held to avoid exacerbating diarrhea. Chronic medications for ulcer prophylaxis, pain, mood/anxiety, insomnia, and hyperlipidemia were continued (iron held inpatient due to nausea), and she improved to tolerating oral intake without further vomiting and was discharged home ambulatory with follow-up for nutrition and possible future G-tube removal.
